Local Tastes
Flat White
A short espresso topped with velvety micro-foamed milk, stronger and less frothy than a cappuccino — a New Zealand invention now served the world over.
Amano · Espresso Workshop
Pavlova
A meringue-based cake with a crisp shell and marshmallow-soft centre, piled with whipped cream and passionfruit or kiwifruit — the fought-over trans-Tasman dessert, claimed by both New Zealand and Australia.
Depot Eatery & Oyster Bar
Food Delivery
Uber Eats
Foreign number: accepted. — a foreign-registered account carries over unchanged, and a new sign-up's code arrives by SMS on most carriers.
Auckland's largest delivery platform by restaurant count, from CBD fine dining to suburban takeaways, with live courier tracking and the same app used for Uber rides. Surge pricing applies on delivery fees at peak times.
ubereats.com/nz
DoorDash
Foreign number: accepted. — sign-up takes an international mobile number and the SMS verification code reaches foreign carriers.
Uber Eats' main Auckland rival, with strong coverage from the North Shore down to the southern suburbs and frequent first-order promotions. Restaurant selection skews slightly smaller than Uber Eats in the CBD core.
doordash.com

Getting Around
Uber
Foreign number: accepted. — a foreign-registered account works unchanged in Auckland, and a new sign-up's verification code arrives by SMS on most international carriers.
Auckland's dominant ride app with wide CBD coverage; upfront fares shown before booking. Surge pricing on Friday and Saturday nights and around Sky Tower during major events.
uber.com/nz
YourRide
Foreign number: accepted. — sign-up takes an international mobile number and the SMS verification code reaches foreign carriers.
New Zealand-owned app booking licensed taxis — Auckland Co-op Taxis and Blue Star among them — rather than rideshare drivers, useful as a backup whenever Uber surges or a metered fare is needed instead.
yourride.nz

Worth Knowing

Auckland is a city built on volcanoes, wrapped in two harbours

Auckland sits on a volcanic field of around 50 cones, most of them climbable in twenty minutes and free — Mount Eden and One Tree Hill are two of the best, and locals will point you to a dozen more.

The city spans two harbours on two different seas: the Waitematā on the Pacific side, where the CBD and Viaduct sit, and the Manukau on the Tasman side, to the south — a fact that surprises most first-time visitors and explains why east-coast and west-coast beaches are both a short drive away.

Ferries are the easy win. A same-day return to Devonport or Waiheke Island needs no booking ahead — just walk onto the Downtown Ferry Terminal and buy at the gate — and both are genuinely worth a full day, not a rushed half-day add-on.

Weather turns fast. Auckland's maritime climate can run four seasons in a day regardless of month; a light rain layer is worth packing even in summer, and outdoor plans — especially the ferry islands — benefit from a loose, weather-flexible itinerary.

Tipping is not expected. Restaurant bills do not carry a service charge and staff are paid a living wage — a rounded-up bill or 10% for exceptional service is a genuine bonus, not an obligation.
